title: A short survey for devs to give your thoughts on generative text in gamedev
author: ChromaGolem

comments.author: ChromaGolem
comments.body:
Hey again! With Steam's awesome news this week this seems like a great time to get a pulse on how the industry (and, specifically, devs) feel about AI text generation in games in general, where we would put the quality at, and what tasks we're using it for in our process. I put together a hopefully-super-quick survey that I'd really appreciate your thoughts on if you have a moment to spare and are using text generation (or are just open to using text generation) in your game(s).

I'd also be more than happy to share the results if there is interest. Thank you!

comments.author: featherless_fiend
comments.body:
Personally I don't think I would ever want to make a live game myself, for now I would stick with pre-generated content. Live games cost extra money to run and have an expiration date, somewhat similar to the issues with multiplayer games.

That's just me though, [good live games](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vVvV5FUcu8I) are possible to make.

I may be interested in pre-generating text and dialogue. There's no extra cost there or expiration date on your game. And if you think about it; a live game is like picking the first result from an AI Art Generator, what if instead you generate 1000 results and pick the best ones yourself? Intentionally crafting your dialogue and story could increase the quality of your game a lot.

replies.author: No_Industry9653
replies.body:
IMO the future is going to be games with local models, they are now getting powerful enough on normal hardware that it's going to be viable to do really cool stuff without the burden of having to be an internet connected service that has a per-use cost.

Games have not yet gone beyond scratching the surface here, I see so much more that could be done than just automating the creation of traditional dialogue trees. Like imagine a game where you can give natural language instructions to an NPC, and the game generates code on the fly to carry out those instructions. Or a system controlling the overarching story, applying narrative tropes dynamically to fit what you have said and done into an interesting and meaningful story. Or a system that can see when you are frustrated with a game interface and highlights things and provides intelligent backseat assistance on request.
